name: Sistrans
kurzbeschreibung: Charming residential village nestled in the foothills, offering breathtaking views of the Tuxer Alpen and the Patscherkofel.
text:
Overview

Sistrans is located at an altitude of 919 meters on the sun-blessed terrace of the Southeastern Low Mountain Range (Südöstliches Mittelgebirge) in the Innsbruck-Land district, just seven kilometers southeast of Tyrol's capital city Innsbruck at the base of Mount Patscherkofel (2,246 m). Home to approximately 2,300 residents, the municipality encompasses the historic village center alongside the hamlets of Tigls, Starkenbühel, and dispersed traditional farmsteads. Enjoying over 2,000 hours of annual sunshine, Sistrans offers sweeping panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley and the limestone crags of the Nordkette in the Karwendel Alps. Preserving a quiet residential charm and rural tranquility, the village functions as an authentic haven for walkers, mountain bikers, and nature lovers seeking relaxation away from mass tourism.

History

The sunny glacial plateau above Innsbruck ranks among Tyrol’s oldest continuously inhabited cultural landscapes. Prehistoric farming settlements flourished here during the Bronze and Iron Ages, as the elevated topography offered protection against periodic river flooding of the Inn while providing fertile soils, documented by the nearby Goldbichl cult sanctuary. Sistrans was first recorded between 1050 and 1065 in the records of Brixen Abbey as in loco Sistrans. For centuries attached to the ancient parish of Patsch and Wilten Abbey, it was elevated to a full parish in 1891. The parish church of Saint Gertrude of Nivelles was first mentioned in 1339. Originally late Gothic, the sanctuary received an exquisite Baroque remodeling between 1727 and 1741, highlighted by Rococo stuccowork by Kassian Singer and Johann Mussak, alongside ceiling frescoes by Josef Anton Kirchebner painted in 1786.

Getting there

Sistrans enjoys rapid transport connections to Innsbruck. By car, exit the A12 Inntal motorway at Innsbruck-Mitte or Innsbruck-Ost and follow the L32 state road via Aldrans up onto the plateau in just ten minutes. Arriving from the south via the A13 Brenner motorway, take the Patsch/Innsbruck-Süd exit and proceed through Lans. International rail travelers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station. VVT regional bus line 530 operates regular services directly connecting the central station to Sistrans village square. In addition, the historic Mittelgebirgsbahn (tram line 6) winds its way through pine forests from Innsbruck to the Lans-Sistrans station, offering a scenic journey.

Tips

Hike up to the popular Sistranser Alm alpine hut at 1,608 meters, accessible via forest trails or official mountain bike route 501, and unwind on the panoramic terrace with traditional Tyrolean dumplings. From the hut, extend your excursion along the scenic Alpine Pasture Circuit connecting the Aldranser Alm and Rinner Alm. Nearby, the Patscherkofel cable car gives access to the celebrated Zirbenweg stone pine trail. For a gentle valley walk, climb the Starkenbühel moraine knoll for unobstructed vistas over the Karwendel peaks, or visit the nearby Lanser See bathing lake and natural lily pond in neighboring Lans.
